title: "`r params$title`"
date: "`r format(Sys.Date(), '%d %B %Y')`"
params:
  store: ""
  title: "Database inventory and column profile"
format:
  html:
    toc: true
    toc-depth: 2
    embed-resources: true

```{r setup}
#| echo: false
# chunk defaults set here as well as in the YAML so the rmarkdown fallback matches Quarto
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(DBinventory)
st <- store_open(params$store)
tables  <- store_read(st, "inventory_tables")
columns <- store_read(st, "inventory_columns")
profile <- store_read(st, "column_profile")
log     <- store_read(st, "profile_log")
meta    <- store_read(st, "run_meta")
store_close(st)
if (is.null(profile)) profile <- DBinventory:::empty_profile()
if (is.null(log)) log <- data.frame(status = character())
has_dt <- requireNamespace("DT", quietly = TRUE)
library(ggplot2)
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1)))
fill_blue <- "#4C78A8"
fill_orange <- "#F58518"
show <- function(x, ...) {
  if (has_dt) DT::datatable(x, rownames = FALSE, filter = "top", extensions = "Buttons",
                            options = list(pageLength = 15, scrollX = TRUE, dom = "Bfrtip", buttons = c("csv", "copy")), ...)
  else knitr::kable(utils::head(x, 200))
}
fmt <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE)
bytes <- function(b) ifelse(is.na(b), "", ifelse(b >= 1e9, paste0(round(b / 1e9, 1), " GB"),
         ifelse(b >= 1e6, paste0(round(b / 1e6, 1), " MB"), paste0(round(b / 1e3), " kB"))))
```

```{r headline, results="asis"}
n_err <- sum(log$status == "error")
cat(sprintf(
  "**%s** tables and views, **%s** columns, **%s** rows in total%s. Profiled %s columns in %s tables%s.\n\n",
  fmt(nrow(tables)), fmt(nrow(columns)), fmt(sum(tables$row_count, na.rm = TRUE)),
  if (any(!is.na(tables$size_bytes))) sprintf(", %s on disk", bytes(sum(tables$size_bytes, na.rm = TRUE))) else "",
  fmt(nrow(profile)), fmt(length(unique(paste(profile$table_schema, profile$table_name)))),
  if (n_err > 0) sprintf("; **%d tables failed** (see the run log)", n_err) else ""
))
if (!is.null(meta) && nrow(meta) > 0) {
  m <- meta[nrow(meta), ]
  cat(sprintf("Last run started %s UTC against `%s` (%s dialect), sampling tables above %s rows, top %d values per column, literal values %s.\n\n",
      m$started_at, m$source, m$dialect, fmt(m$sample_rows), m$top_n,
      if (isTRUE(as.logical(m$keep_values))) "kept" else "suppressed for identifiers, free text and personal-data names"))
}
```

## Tables

Ranked by row count. `newest_datetime` is the latest value in any date or datetime column, the freshness signal. Tables with no datetime column show blank.

```{r tables}
t <- tables[order(-ifelse(is.na(tables$row_count), -1, tables$row_count)), ]
t$size <- bytes(t$size_bytes)
cols <- intersect(c("table_schema", "table_name", "table_type", "n_columns", "row_count", "size", "newest_datetime", "newest_datetime_column"), names(t))
show(as.data.frame(t[, cols]))
```

### Freshness

```{r freshness, fig.height=4}
fresh <- tables[!is.na(tables$newest_datetime), ]
d <- if (nrow(fresh) > 0) as.Date(substr(fresh$newest_datetime, 1, 10)) else as.Date(character())
d <- d[!is.na(d)]
if (length(d) > 0) {
  month_start <- function(x) as.Date(format(x, "%Y-%m-01"))
  months <- seq(month_start(min(d)), month_start(max(d)), by = "month")
  edges <- seq(months[1], by = "month", length.out = length(months) + 1)   # month boundaries
  counts <- data.frame(
    from = edges[-length(edges)], to = edges[-1],
    tables = as.integer(table(factor(month_start(d), levels = as.character(months))))
  )
  step <- max(1, ceiling(length(edges) / 13))        # at most about thirteen boundary labels
  ggplot(counts) +
    geom_rect(aes(xmin = from, xmax = to, ymin = 0, ymax = tables), fill = fill_blue, colour = "white") +
    scale_x_date(breaks = edges[seq(1, length(edges), by = step)], date_labels = "%d %b %Y", expand = expansion(0)) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = function(l) unique(floor(pretty(l))), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
    labs(x = "Newest datetime in table (bars span the month between two boundaries)", y = "Tables")
} else cat("No datetime columns found, so no freshness to show.")
```

### Row counts

Bins are log-spaced so that reference tables and multi-million-row logs both show; each bar covers the row counts between the two boundaries it sits on. Bars are not equal widths because 1 to 2 and 5 to 10 each double, while 2 to 5 is a factor of 2.5.

```{r rows, fig.height=4}
rc <- tables$row_count[!is.na(tables$row_count) & tables$row_count > 0]
if (length(rc) > 0) {
  lo <- floor(log10(min(rc)))
  hi <- ceiling(log10(max(rc)))
  if (hi == lo) hi <- lo + 1
  edges <- sort(unique(as.vector(outer(c(1, 2, 5), 10^seq(lo, hi)))))   # 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, ...
  edges <- edges[edges <= 10^hi]
  bins <- cut(rc, breaks = edges, right = FALSE, include.lowest = TRUE)
  counts <- data.frame(from = edges[-length(edges)], to = edges[-1], tables = as.integer(table(bins)))
  ggplot(counts) +
    geom_rect(aes(xmin = from, xmax = to, ymin = 0, ymax = tables), fill = fill_blue, colour = "white") +
    scale_x_log10(breaks = edges, labels = scales::label_comma(), expand = expansion(0)) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = function(l) unique(floor(pretty(l))), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
    labs(x = "Rows in table (bars span the range between two boundaries)", y = "Tables")
}
```

## Columns

### Type mix

```{r types}
tc <- as.data.frame(table(type_class = columns$type_class), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
tc <- tc[order(-tc$Freq), ]
names(tc)[2] <- "columns"
knitr::kable(tc, row.names = FALSE)
```

### Inferred semantic types

A first draft: `identifier`, `code`, `category`, `flag`, `date`, `datetime`, `free_text`, `count`, `measure`, `constant`, `empty`. For a person to confirm, not a finding.

```{r semantic}
if (nrow(profile) > 0) {
  sem <- as.data.frame(table(semantic_type = profile$semantic_type), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  sem <- sem[order(-sem$Freq), ]
  names(sem)[2] <- "columns"
  knitr::kable(sem, row.names = FALSE)
}
```

### Nulls and uniqueness

```{r nulls, fig.height=4}
if (nrow(profile) > 0) {
  rates <- rbind(
    data.frame(measure = "Null rate", rate = profile$null_rate),
    data.frame(measure = "Distinct rate (distinct / non-null)", rate = profile$distinct_rate)
  )
  rates <- rates[!is.na(rates$rate), ]
  rates$measure <- factor(rates$measure, levels = c("Null rate", "Distinct rate (distinct / non-null)"))
  ggplot(rates, aes(x = rate, fill = measure)) +
    geom_histogram(breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.05), colour = "white", show.legend = FALSE) +
    facet_wrap(~ measure, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(fill_blue, fill_orange)) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.25), labels = scales::label_percent()) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Columns") +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5))
}
```

```{r empties, results="asis"}
if (nrow(profile) > 0) {
  empty <- profile[profile$semantic_type %in% c("empty", "constant"), ]
  cat(sprintf("**%d** columns are entirely null and **%d** hold a single constant value: candidates to drop from any dictionary.\n\n",
      sum(profile$semantic_type == "empty"), sum(profile$semantic_type == "constant")))
}
```

## Candidate duplicate columns

Columns in different tables with the same value fingerprint (type, distinct-count magnitude, min, max and top values). A starting point for the duplicate map, not a verdict: value-overlap tests come next.

```{r dupes}
if (nrow(profile) > 0) {
  dup <- as.data.frame(duplicate_candidates(profile))
  if (nrow(dup) > 0) {
    dup$columns <- vapply(strsplit(dup$columns, "; ", fixed = TRUE), function(cols) {
      paste(if (has_dt) htmltools::htmlEscape(cols) else cols, collapse = if (has_dt) "<br>" else "; ")
    }, character(1))
    show(dup, escape = setdiff(seq_along(dup), which(names(dup) == "columns")))
  } else cat("No cross-table fingerprint matches.")
}
```

## Column profile

`top_values` lists the most frequent values with their counts; blank where values are suppressed or the column has too many distinct values for a frequency table to be useful.

```{r profile}
if (nrow(profile) > 0) {
  p <- profile
  p$null_rate <- round(p$null_rate, 3)
  p$distinct_rate <- round(p$distinct_rate, 3)
  p$mean_value <- round(p$mean_value, 3)
  p$mean_length <- round(p$mean_length, 1)
  p$top_values <- vapply(p$top_values, function(j) {
    if (is.na(j)) return("")
    tv <- jsonlite::fromJSON(j)
    items <- paste0(if (has_dt) htmltools::htmlEscape(tv$value) else tv$value, " (", format(tv$n, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE), ")")
    paste(items, collapse = if (has_dt) ";<br>" else "; ")
  }, character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)
  cols <- c("table_schema", "table_name", "column_name", "data_type", "semantic_type", "row_count", "null_rate",
            "distinct_count", "distinct_rate", "is_unique", "min_value", "max_value", "mean_value", "top_values", "sampled")
  p <- as.data.frame(p[, intersect(cols, names(p))])
  # every column is HTML-escaped except top_values, whose values were escaped above
  show(p, escape = setdiff(seq_along(p), which(names(p) == "top_values")))
}
```

## Run log

One row per table per profiling attempt, with its outcome, how long it took and any error message. It is the checkpoint: a rerun against the same store skips tables whose latest entry is `ok` and retries the rest. Errors here usually mean a broken view or an object the login cannot read.

```{r log}
if (nrow(log) > 0) {
  l <- log[order(log$logged_at, decreasing = TRUE), ]
  l$seconds <- round(l$seconds, 1)
  show(as.data.frame(l))
}
```
